holidays.name: National Kite Flying Day
holidays.description: A day for taking a kite outside and letting the wind do the work. Grab a diamond kite, a box kite, or a dollar-store dragon. Then run across a field while pretending you meant to look that ridiculous.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that grew out of the American kite-flying community. It is celebrated every year on February 8. The day honors one of the oldest forms of human flight, which dates back thousands of years.
holidays.funFact: Kites were used in early scientific experiments, including Benjamin Franklin's famous stormy-sky electricity experiment. Kites have also been used to carry fishing lines, send messages, and lift cameras.

holidays.name: National Molasses Bar Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the chewy, spiced, gloriously sticky molasses bar. Bake a batch with ginger and cinnamon, then enjoy a sweet treat with a deep, dark, old-fashioned flavor.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday of unclear origin. It is observed every February 8 and celebrates a classic American baked treat made with molasses, a syrup left over from refining sugarcane.
holidays.funFact: Molasses is a byproduct of sugar-making. Its flavor and color depend on how many times the sugarcane juice has been boiled, and the darkest kind, blackstrap, is the most intense.

holidays.name: Propose Day
holidays.description: The second day of Valentine's Week is set aside for declaring your feelings. People use it to pop the question or to confess a crush. Some go big with a ring, and others write a heartfelt note.
holidays.origin: Propose Day is part of the Valentine's Week tradition, which is especially popular in India and South Asia. Each day of the week from February 7 to 14 has its own theme. February 8 is the day for proposals.
holidays.funFact: Propose Day is the second of eight themed days that lead up to Valentine's Day. The week starts with Rose Day on February 7, and the days that follow include Chocolate Day, Teddy Day, and Promise Day.
